lessons.title: Séimhiú agus -fadh / -feadh
lessons.rule: To say what someone would do, put séimhiú on the verb and add -fadh to a broad root or -feadh to a slender root: glan becomes ghlanfadh sé, cuir becomes chuirfeadh sé. L, n, r and sc, sp, st, sm take no séimhiú (lasfadh, rithfeadh).
steps: Find the root: glan.
Add séimhiú: ghlan.
The last vowel is broad (a), so add -fadh: ghlanfadh.
Put the verb first: Ghlanfadh sé an scáileán.

more.answer: Chuirfeadh sé an mála sa charr.

items.prompt: (Rith) sé go dtí an stad bus.
items.answer: Rithfeadh sé go dtí an stad bus.

lessons.title: D' roimh ghuta agus roimh f
lessons.en: D' before a vowel and before f
lessons.rule: If the verb begins with a vowel, put d' in front of it (ól becomes d'ólfadh sé); if it begins with f, add séimhiú and put d' in front (fan becomes d'fhanfadh sé).
steps: Find the root: ól.
It begins with a vowel, so put d' in front: d'ól.
Add -fadh (broad): d'ólfadh.
Put the verb first: D'ólfadh sé an t-uisce.

more.answer: D'fhágfadh sé an fón sa mhála.

items.answer: D'fhanfadh sé ag an stad bus.

lessons.title: An fhoirm dhiúltach: Ní
lessons.rule: Put Ní before the verb, keep the séimhiú and drop any d': Mholfadh muid becomes Ní mholfadh muid, D'éistfidís becomes Ní éistfidís.
steps: Start with the positive verb: D'éistfidís.
Drop the d': éistfidís.
Put Ní in front: Ní éistfidís.

lessons.title: Freagra: -fainn / -finn
lessons.rule: When the question asks tú (-fá / -feá), answer with mé: add -fainn to a broad root or -finn to a slender root, with séimhiú or d' for yes and Ní for no (Chaithfinn nó ní chaithfinn).
steps: Find the root in the question: an gcaithfeá has the root caith.
Add séimhiú and -finn (slender) for yes: Chaithfinn.
Put ní before it for no: ní chaithfinn.
Fill both gaps: Chaithfinn nó ní chaithfinn.

example.answer: An gcaithfeá an éide scoile? Chaithfinn nó ní chaithfinn.

lessons.title: Dá: an modh coinníollach sa dá leath
lessons.en: Dá: the conditional in both halves
lessons.rule: After dá (if), both halves of the sentence use the conditional: Dá mbeadh tart orm, d'ólfainn tae. Work out the person from the dá half (orm, mo, mbeinn all point to mé).
steps: Read the dá half to find the person: orm, so mé.
Put the verb in the conditional with the mé ending: cuir becomes chuirfinn.
Write the whole sentence: Dá mbeadh an lá fliuch, chuirfinn cóta fearthainne orm.

example.prompt: Dá mbeadh an lá fliuch, (cuir) cóta fearthainne orm.
example.answer: Dá mbeadh an lá fliuch, chuirfinn cóta fearthainne orm.

lessons.title: Cad é a dhéanfá?
lessons.rule: Answer Cad é a dhéanfá? with a verb in the conditional with the mé ending, and Cad é a dhéanfadh sé / sí / siad? with the same person (dhéanfainn, ghlanfadh sí, d'amharcfaidís).
steps: Read the question: dhéanfá asks about tú, so answer with mé.
Choose a verb: ól.
Put it in the conditional with the mé ending: D'ólfainn gloine uisce.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -faí
lessons.rule: When no one is named (it would be done), add -faí to a broad root, with séimhiú or d' as usual: mol becomes mholfaí, ól becomes d'ólfaí.
steps: Find the root: mol.
Add séimhiú: mhol.
The root is broad, so add -faí: mholfaí.
Put the verb first: Mholfaí na gasúir dá mbeidís ciúin.

example.answer: Mholfaí na gasúir dá mbeidís ciúin.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -fí
lessons.rule: With a slender root, add -fí instead, with séimhiú or d' as usual: cuir becomes chuirfí, éist becomes d'éistfí.
steps: Find the root: caith.
Add séimhiú: chaith.
The root is slender, so add -fí: chaithfí.
Put the verb first: Chaithfí an éide scoile.
